root_cause.text: A reversed boolean condition in fs/super.c:filesystems_freeze_callback() misinterpreted freeze_all_ptr, causing the power-management filesystem freeze path to freeze all superblocks when filesystem_freeze_enabled was false instead of restricting freezing to FS_POWER_FREEZE filesystems.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))` to `if (!freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state the original check was reversed and "causes all file systems to be frozen when filesystem_freeze_enabled is false."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `if (freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))` to `if (!freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE))`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state the original check was reversed and "causes all file systems to be frozen when filesystem_freeze_enabled is false."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix filesystem freeze callback logic so `FS_POWER_FREEZE` filtering applies only to non-freeze-all operations.
intent_record.what: The condition in `filesystems_freeze_callback()` was changed from `if (freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE)) return;` to `if (!freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE)) return;`, inverting the `freeze_all_ptr` check while keeping the filesystem flag check unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the skip logic so that when a full freeze-all operation is requested, filesystems are no longer incorrectly excluded for lacking `FS_POWER_FREEZE`; instead, that flag is only required when `freeze_all_ptr` is not set. This fixes which superblocks are eligible to be frozen in different freeze modes.

grouping_result.intent: Fix filesystem freeze callback logic so `FS_POWER_FREEZE` filtering applies only to non-freeze-all operations.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the freeze callback boolean logic around freeze-all versus FS_POWER_FREEZE filtering, which matches the root cause of the reversed condition causing the wrong set of superblocks to be frozen.

candidates.rationale: This condition is the root cause: it applies FS_POWER_FREEZE filtering when freeze_all_ptr is true, which is the reverse of the intended logic. As a result, when filesystem_freeze_enabled is false and the operation should restrict freezing to FS_POWER_FREEZE filesystems, the filter is skipped and all superblocks may be frozen.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional reverses the intended meaning of freeze_all_ptr. It applies the FS_POWER_FREEZE restriction when freeze_all_ptr is true, instead of when freezing is not for all filesystems. That inversion causes the power-management freeze path to skip the restriction and freeze all superblocks when filesystem_freeze_enabled is false.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in the shown function body and call site. The callback now takes `void *freeze_all_ptr` instead of `void *unused`, and it contains the gating check `if (freeze_all_ptr && !(sb->s_type->fs_flags & FS_POWER_FREEZE)) return;`. This means when the pointer is non-NULL, only filesystems with `FS_POWER_FREEZE` are frozen; otherwise all eligible superblocks are processed. The caller `filesystems_freeze(bool freeze_all)` sets `freeze_all_ptr = &freeze_all` only when `freeze_all` is true, and passes `NULL` otherwise. That is the correct non-reversed interpretation of the boolean state, so the vulnerable construct described in the root cause (misinterpreting `freeze_all_ptr` so that `filesystem_freeze_enabled == false` caused freezing all superblocks instead of restricting to `FS_POWER_FREEZE`) is not present here. Therefore this code already contains the fix.
